newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close higher on rebound.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close higher on rebound.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed higher on Friday as Thursday's losses triggered buying from investors sanguine about the market's immediate outlook, brokers said.
The weighted index, which climbed to a high of 7,313.08 earlier in the session, encountered some profit-taking in late trade but still closed 28.46 points or 0.39 percent higher at 7,248.01.
Turnover was a hectic T$95.84 billion.
Electronic shares, sparked by computer giant Acer Inc's overnight purchase of Texas Instruments Corp's notebook computer division, rose 1.85 percent to lead to rebound.
Acer, the third most actively traded issue, gained T$1.50 to finish at T$24.10.

"More buyers were drawn into the market following Thursday's fall, indicating that investors still feel good about the market's potential for further gains," said George Hou, a fund manager at Jardine Fleming.
On Thursday the index had tumbled 71.22 points or nearly one percent as profit-taking swept a market which before that session had risen more than 400 points in January.
The construction sector gained 1.11 percent on Friday on hopes that Taiwan's current economic recovery would lift the real estate industry out of its prolonged slump.
Brokers expected the index to challenge for a higher upside in the near term, with more buyers likely to enter the market before the Chinese lunar new year on February 7.
A 7,220-7,310 range was seen for Saturday.
